name: The Roman World at the Time of Christ
path: New Testament Studies: Life and Doctrine in Christ

objectives.text: Identify a Roman soldier or centurion in a Bible story such as the centurion who asked Jesus to heal his servant
Recall that Caesar Augustus ruled the Roman Empire and ordered the census that brought Mary and Joseph to Bethlehem
Describe how Roman roads and sea routes helped travelers like Paul move from city to city
Explain what Jesus taught when he was shown a Roman coin bearing Caesar's image
Summarize the Pax Romana and describe how it made travel and trade safer across the empire
Explain why Jewish tax collectors working for Rome were despised, using the account of Zacchaeus
Describe crucifixion as a Roman punishment and identify the Roman officials and soldiers involved in Jesus' death
Compare the roles of Pilate as Roman governor and Herod Antipas as a client ruler in the trial of Jesus
Distinguish the members of the Herodian family who appear in the New Testament and their relationship to Rome
Explain how Koine Greek as a common language of the Roman world helped the gospel spread among many peoples
Describe Greco-Roman polytheism and identify the pagan gods and temple practices the apostles encountered in Acts
Explain the Reformed teaching that God in his providence prepared the Roman world for the coming of Christ in the fullness of time
Analyze how Roman roads, peace, and law contributed to the course of Paul's missionary journeys
Explain how Luke dates the events of Jesus' life by naming Roman rulers and officials
Explain the imperial cult and why refusing to honor Caesar as divine placed early Christians in danger
Analyze how Paul used his Roman citizenship and legal rights in the course of his ministry
Explain the social hierarchy of the Roman world, including citizens, freedmen, and slaves, and how apostolic teaching addressed it
Analyze how Paul engaged Stoic and Epicurean philosophers at Athens
Construct an annotated map of the Roman provinces where key New Testament events took place
Explain the Roman destruction of Jerusalem in AD 70 and how Jesus foretold it
Analyze how apostolic commands to submit to governing authorities applied to Christians living under Roman rule
Analyze the Roman patronage system and its bearing on New Testament teaching about benefactors and service
Evaluate the conflict between the Christian confession that Jesus is Lord and the claims of Caesar
Write an analysis of how Roman political, social, and religious structures shape the narrative of a Gospel or Acts

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies: soldiers, Caesar, roads, the coin, Pax Romana, tax collectors, Pilate and Herod, Greek, infrastructure, imperial cult, citizenship, social hierarchy, map, Jesus is Lord versus Caesar, patronage, and the synthesis. Turned the observation and research tasks into assessable competencies. Added objectives on crucifixion, the Herodian family, Greco-Roman religion, providential preparation (Galatians 4:4), Luke's Roman dating, Paul at Athens, the fall of Jerusalem in AD 70, and submission to authorities under Rome. Anchored each to specific verses and added confessional references only where they state the doctrine taught.
